note.title: Practical methods and conclusions
note.overview: A conclusion states what results show; an explanation gives the scientific reason. High-quality responses use evidence.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 vocabulary for practical methods and conclusions.
Apply the knowledge rather than relying on recognition alone.
Use the command word and include every required scientific point.
mustMemoriseRules: Food tests, pondweed, leaf starch, mineral-deficiency and competition practicals each need specific controls.
A good conclusion includes a pattern and data reference.
An explanation links the pattern to biological mechanism.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: a statement of what the results show, including the pattern and evidence
a scientific reason accounting for the observed pattern
another measurement used to assess consistency and calculate a mean
a change making a result more precise or accurate without changing the intended variable

workedExamples.answer: The conclusion states the pattern; the explanation gives the biological reason for it.
workedExamples.why: Explain biological ideas as linked steps: name the structure or process, state what happens, and connect it to the effect on the cell, organism or ecosystem. Use precise scientific terms rather than everyday substitutes.
